quarterly_data.signal: CFO Yoshio Takegawa (prepared remarks), first half (cumulative Q2) FY2026: net sales JPY 1,100.6 billion, up JPY 105.1 billion year-on-year - lower architectural glass shipments in Europe and the Americas were more than offset by yen depreciation, higher shipments in Essential Chemicals Southeast Asia, Integrated Chemicals and electronic materials, and pricing policies in Integrated Chemicals and European architectural glass. Operating profit JPY 64.7 billion, up JPY 10.6 billion despite higher manufacturing cost; profit before tax JPY 60.3 billion, up JPY 26.6 billion (foreign exchange gains, non-recurrence of Biopharmaceuticals CDMO impairment losses); profit attributable to owners of the parent up JPY 21.6 billion to JPY 35.5 billion. Strategic businesses: net sales JPY 264.4 billion (up JPY 28.7 billion), operating profit JPY 35 billion (up JPY 12 billion), 54% of group operating profit. H1 capex JPY 90.1 billion (down JPY 6.8 billion), depreciation and amortization JPY 97.8 billion, R&D JPY 28.8 billion; operating cash flow JPY 194.9 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 net sales JPY 1,100.6 billion (up JPY 105.1 billion); operating profit JPY 64.7 billion (up JPY 10.6 billion); profit attributable to owners JPY 35.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Yoshio Takegawa: the full-year FY2026 outlook announced in February remains unchanged, including the segment outlooks and the capex / depreciation / R&D plan (capex planned to fall by JPY 61.3 billion year-over-year); the crude oil price assumption was revised from $70 to $100 US per barrel at the Q1 results in May. Strategic businesses full-year outlook kept at net sales JPY 560 billion (up JPY 58.5 billion) and operating profit JPY 80 billion (up JPY 21.3 billion). The first half was slightly better than projections, but 'many uncertainties remaining. We don't have clear visibility into the second half yet, and that is the reason why we did not change our full-year forecast'; he sees no particular risk, and the business remains second-half oriented toward the JPY 150 billion full-year operating profit. Q3: overall net sales about the same level as Q2 (Electronics and Chemicals up seasonally, Automotive and Life Science lower), with operating profit growth expected in Automotive and especially Electronics. The Middle East situation's impact on full-year earnings is expected to remain limited (diversified procurement, price adjustments).
quarterly_data.figure: full-year outlook unchanged; JPY 150 billion full-year operating profit; strategic businesses net sales JPY 560 billion and operating profit JPY 80 billion; capex down JPY 61.3 billion year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics segment H1 (prepared remarks): net sales up JPY 6.2 billion to JPY 174.4 billion, operating profit down JPY 5.7 billion to JPY 18.7 billion. Display was flat (higher LCD glass substrate prices offset by lower specialty display glass shipments from a planned business exit); Electronic materials net sales rose JPY 5.9 billion as shipments of EUVL mask blanks are in a recovery trend and other semiconductor-related materials and optoelectronic materials increased; segment profit fell on higher manufacturing costs and the negative yen-depreciation impact on display. Operating profit split: display 30%, Electronic materials 70%. Chemicals segment: net sales up JPY 46.2 billion to JPY 322 billion, operating profit up JPY 5.6 billion to JPY 28.2 billion; Integrated Chemicals net sales up JPY 19.8 billion on higher sales prices and increased shipments of products for semiconductor and other electronic applications. CFO Takegawa: Integrated Chemicals profit improved on an ethylene-shortage-driven rise in selling prices and on semiconductor-related demand - smartphone, PC, data center and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Second-half outlook: shipments of semiconductor-related materials such as EUVL mask blanks, and of Integrated Chemicals products for the electronic sector, are expected to increase.
quarterly_data.figure: Electronics net sales JPY 174.4 billion, operating profit JPY 18.7 billion; Electronic materials net sales up JPY 5.9 billion; Integrated Chemicals net sales up JPY 19.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Yoshinori Hirai on the semiconductor growth strategy: electronics and Performance Chemicals focus on products for semiconductor manufacturing, front-end processes and also back-end packaging. With AI and data-center demand expected to keep growing, AGC has already made the capacity-expansion investment decisions for EUV mask blanks, CMP slurry and 'ion lens materials for lithography equipment', expecting capacity expansion of 20% to 50% by 2028 (management: the investment is 'double digits JPY billion'; for EUV blanks Hirai says a 30% increase in volume is in mind, comparable to the 2023 expansion); KrF and ArF conventional applications also serve diversified semiconductor demand. Semiconductor-related sales were about JPY 100 billion in 2025 across electronics and Performance Chemicals, targeted to double to a JPY 200 billion scale by 2030, with packaging materials and other new products to be developed and launched by 2030. Hirai: customer evaluation and adoption of new CCL products is 'proceeding steadily'; CMP slurry (consumables) sales volume is increasing.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor-related sales about JPY 100 billion in 2025, target JPY 200 billion scale by 2030; capacity expansion of 20% to 50% by 2028; EUV blanks 30% increase in volume in mind

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Yoshinori Hirai on EUVL mask blanks: last year supply to AGC's major customers dropped; that is now improving and shipments to other customers are also increasing. 'Frankly speaking, from our customers, we are getting very strong order inquiries and request for more supplies... the way we see it, the supply is getting tighter.' This year's volume already exceeds last year's and a further increase is expected next year; the production line is already being expanded and further investment has been decided. Net sales will not return to the record 2024 level immediately - 2024 was 'a special year' with fast growth and high unit prices, and the average price is lower now as the market matured - but 'next year we will definitely exceed 2024 and return to growth trajectory.' The mix is shifting toward more challenging, higher-grade products with a higher unit price but also higher cost. Of EUV inquiries and actual production and shipment, the 'absolute majority of that is logic, not memory. Logic is moving faster than memory.'
quarterly_data.figure: EUVL mask blank volume this year already above last year; net sales expected to exceed 2024 next year

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments H1 (prepared remarks): Architectural glass net sales JPY 229.3 billion (up JPY 18.5 billion), operating profit JPY 8.5 billion (up JPY 5.5 billion); Automotive net sales JPY 280.3 billion (up JPY 24.6 billion), operating profit JPY 13.3 billion (down JPY 1.8 billion) on higher manufacturing costs in Europe and the Americas, which CFO Takegawa attributes to internal production-facility issues; Life Science net sales JPY 72.3 billion (up JPY 8.8 billion), operating loss improved by JPY 5.9 billion to JPY 6.1 billion after closing the Biopharmaceuticals CDMO Colorado site. CFO Takegawa: Life Science expected to turn profitable in Q4 as Copenhagen orders, production and deliveries start; the Colorado divestiture is targeted before the end of this fiscal year; the new long-term contract at the Yokohama site alone secures close to 50% of its capacity utilization. CEO Hirai: AGC Biologics' Yokohama site expects GMP commercial production to start by 2027. Display: Hirai says LCD glass prices, conventionally reduced every year, have been increased and panel makers are raising panel prices too; second-half display volume is expected to decrease slightly, and if the exchange rate hovers around JPY 160 to the US dollar AGC will have to ask customers to accept price revisions.
quarterly_data.figure: Architectural glass net sales JPY 229.3 billion; Automotive net sales JPY 280.3 billion; Life Science net sales JPY 72.3 billion, operating loss JPY 6.1 billion
